judgment_text:
Prayer in CMP No. 6909 of 2025: Civil Miscellaneous Petition is filed to condone the delay of 4802 days in filing second appeal against the order passed in As. No. 102/2012 dated 25-8-2012 on the file of the III Additional City Civil Judge, Chennai

Prayer in SA Sr No. 175480 of 2024: second appeal is filed under Section 100 CPC against the order passed in As. No. 102/2012 dated 25-8-2012 on the file of the III Additional City Civil Judge, Chennai, modifying the decree and judgment passed in O.S. No. 11095 of 2009 dated 30-6-2011 by the I Assistant Judge, City Civil Court, Chennai and allow the second appeal

COMMON ORDER

This civil miscellaneous petition has been filed to condone the delay of 4802 days in filing the second appeal against the judgment and decree passed in A.S. No. 102 of 2012 dated 25-8-2012 on the file of III Additional Judge, City Civil Court, Chennai.

2. It is seen from the affidavit filed in support of the petition that the judgment in the first appeal was passed on 25-8-2012 and the second appeal was filed only on 20-12-2024. In the affidavit filed in support of the petition, it was stated by the petitioners that their father was already party to the first appeal and after dismissal of the same, he instructed the earlier counsel to prefer the second appeal and signed the necessary papers. However, the earlier counsel did not file the second appeal and after receipt of notice in the execution proceedings, the petitioners acquired knowledge about the litigation involving his father and decided to to file the present second appeal.

3. The petitioners, as a legal representatives of the deceased father, are bound to the judgment and decree passed by the first appellate court. Though it is stated by the petitioners that their father gave suitable instruction to his counsel to prefer the second appeal immediately and the same has not been preferred, they have not given any reason for the failure of his father or the petitioners to pursue the matter for the past 15 years. The reasons given by the petitioners that they are not aware of the litigation cannot be accepted. If this kind of Explanation offered by the petitioners is accepted, the judgment and decree passed against fore fathers before the number of years will be easily challenged by the descendants by pleading ignorance of the earlier litigation. The petitioners are the beneficiary of the estate of their deceased father and any judgment passed against him is biding on them. In the absence of any plausible Explanation for condoning such inordinate delay of 4802 days, this court is not inclined to accept the prayer made by the petitioner.

4. Accordingly, this civil miscellaneous petition is dismissed. Consequently, the second appeal in SA Sr No. 175480 of 2024 is rejected at the SR stage itself. There shall be no order as to costs.
